backend / Expense Tracker API

Keeping expense records user-scoped

Authentication, persistence and query design in a Spring Boot REST API.

HTTP request → JWT / Spring Security → Controller → Service → JPA → PostgreSQL

The problem

Expense records belong to individual users. A useful expense API needs more than create, read, update and delete endpoints: it also needs authentication, ownership checks and predictable input handling.

Authentication and ownership

The Java 21 / Spring Boot application uses Spring Security and JWT authentication. Passwords are hashed with BCrypt. Expense operations are scoped to the authenticated user, keeping ownership relevant when records are read or changed.

A layered API

Controllers handle HTTP requests and validated data transfer objects. Services contain application operations, and Spring Data JPA / Hibernate handles persistence in PostgreSQL. Global exception handling gives API failures a consistent response path.

Finding the right records

The implementation supports pagination and sorting alongside category, amount and date filtering. These query capabilities make a growing expense history usable without returning every record in a single response.

Testing and running locally

The repository contains JUnit and Mockito service tests, MockMvc authentication tests, and Docker / Docker Compose configuration. GitHub Actions runs a Java 21 build and test workflow with a PostgreSQL 16 service on pushes and pull requests to main. This describes the configured workflow, not a claim that its latest run passed.
